children: The cost of artificial intelligence has been falling faster than that of other transformative technologies in history, according to research from Epoch AI shared by Daily Chartbook.

The chart compares the relative cost of AI with electricity, lithium-ion batteries, computing, and DNA sequencing, with prices adjusted for inflation. AI's cost curve from 2021 to 2026 shows a far steeper decline than the historical trajectories of the other technologies.

The comparison tracks the number of years since each technology's price decline began. Electricity is shown from 1892 to 1973, lithium-ion batteries from 1991 to 2024, computing from 1940 to -2001, and DNA sequencing from 2001 to 2022. The AI series begins in 2021 and drops sharply over the period shown.

The chart's vertical axis measures relative cost on a logarithmic scale, with the decline extending from 10 times at the top to as much as 1 trillion times at the bottom. The AI line falls much more rapidly than the other technology curves over their respective periods.

The chart's caption said the AI series had fallen at 47% per quarter, equivalent to a 12.7-fold decline per year. It cited Epoch AI research for the AI series and noted that the compute series ends earlier simply because newer data was unavailable.
The caption also referenced Appenzeller's 2024 finding that per-token prices for models achieving a given capability had fallen by roughly 10x a year from 2021-24.

The comparison shows the unusually rapid decline in the relative cost of AI performance compared with the historical examples included in the analysis, while the technologies are shown across different times.
